summary: Stream affinity reshuffle triggered large 5xx burst and upstream runtime panics
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10T12:10Z and 2026-03-10T12:40Z we observed a rapid elevation of 5xx errors for a single enterprise tenant (NimbusCommerce) on prod us-east-1. The spike correlated with a control-plane priority/resync operation that pushed a route rewrite for multi-stream affinity. Impact: Customer reporting increased failed chat sessions and long polling errors; their SDK surfaced 502/503 for streaming endpoints. External symptom: <error_rate> rose from baseline 0.09% to 7.8% across the tenant's streaming route; p95 latency climbed from 220ms to 1.2s on some proxy hops. Observed broader noise: a small number of upstream serving-runtime processes received watchdog SIGTERM and later crashed with GPU driver watchdog timeouts.

2026-03-10T12:12Z - Route rewrite pushed to edge fleet (canary fraction 100%)

steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a staging cluster replicate customer workload: long-lived streaming sessions (~1-5min), multiplexed connections and periodic small heartbeats
2)  Inject a priority-resync that performs an affinity rewrite which strips/rewrites the session-affinity header during handoff
3) Observe api-gateway accept queue growth and proxy backlog; runtimes log stream handoff errors and some trigger watchdog restarts

comments: Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10T12:17Z: Customer reported mass 502/503 failures on streaming path; gathering logs and tenant id.
SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-10T12:20Z: Noted control-plane push at 12:12Z. Accept queue and proxy backlog rising; suspect affinity handoff bug - paging routing team.

investigation_notes: Initial triage: correlation between priority-resync/control-plane push and spike start time (12:12Z).
Hypothesis A: routing rewrite stripped multiplex header causing runtime to treat active streams as orphaned during proxy handoff; orphaning triggers prefetch cancellations and rapid socket churn.
Hypothesis B: backpressure on api-gateway accept queue amplified hedged retries from SDKs leading to connection thrash and watchog hits on GPU-heavy runtimes.
Confirmed through packet capture and proxy logs that X-Stream-Affinity header was being rewritten to empty string during handoff in 8% of connections for the tenant's route.
Reproduction in staging: applying the same rewrite produced identical accept queue growth and runtime SIGTERM chain; reverting prevented the failure.
root_cause: A control-plane priority-resync rollout contained a buggy route rewrite that removed the session-multiplex header during proxy handoff. This produced orphaned streaming sessions, accept queue growth, and a retry/amplification loop that caused several serving-runtime watchdog restarts under GPU load.
fixes_applied: Immediate rollback of the routing rewrite (2026-03-10T12:30Z)
Controlled rolling restart of affected edge proxies and a small subset of runtimes (12:31Z-12:38Z)
Hotfix PR submitted to routing service to stop blanking X-Stream-Affinity during handoffs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/787 (merged)
Added a temporary guard in api-gateway: drop handoffs that would strip affinity instead of rewriting them (hotpatch)
Short-term: increased accept queue watermark alerting and tuned hedged retry window for streaming SDKs
resolution: Rollback + controlled restarts reduced the error rate to baseline by 12:36Z. Hotfix PR merged to prevent header blanking and a follow-up config gate added to control-plane to disable affinity rewrites during active tenant sessions. Customer notified of root cause and workaround; agreed to postmortem and permanent mitigation schedule.
next_steps: Postmortem and RCA document (owner: SRE) - due 2026-03-15
Add unit/integration tests in routing service to verify affinity header preservation during handoff (owner: routing eng)
Improve canary policy to include small-production-tenants for affinity-sensitive routes (owner: control-plane)
Update SDK hedged retry docs and add client-side jitter to reduce retry amplification (owner: SDK team)
